//: Shared REST contract for the `node-rest` CapabilityBroker adapter (#2276 slice B). One file, three replayers: packages/webapp/tests/work-unit/capability-rest-adapter.test.ts pins the requests the adapter EMITS; packages/node-server/tests/routes/capability-rest-contract.test.ts and packages/swift-server/Tests/CapabilityRestContractTests.swift replay `serverCases` against a live router so both privileged servers stay on one wire. A route rename on either server, or in the adapter, breaks this file's replayers rather than a float at runtime.
//substitutions: `{{unknownSecret}}` in a path is replaced by the replayer with a name that provably does not exist in that run's store.
//servers: `servers` names which privileged servers must answer an entry; a replayer skips what its server is not listed for. Absent means both. Today exactly one entry is not universal: `POST /api/secrets` (persisted secret creation) exists on node-server and NOT on swift-server. `secrets.set` DEFAULTS to session scope, which works on both, so the gap is only reachable via an explicit `scope: 'persisted'` — the adapter reports that server's 404 as CapabilityUnavailable naming this note, not as a retryable failure. Recorded here rather than hidden so the gap is visible; closing it is issue #2806 (a Keychain-backed write route on swift-server), after which both `servers` markers and this note come out and the existing Swift replayer starts enforcing the two entries with no test changes.

operations.//: Transparent relay: the CALLER's verb is forwarded upstream, so both servers accept any method. The target URL travels in the `X-Target-URL` header, never the path.
Reads the masked list and selects by name — the real value never leaves the server, so there is no plaintext route to pin.
Only reached by an explicit `scope: 'persisted'`; the default session scope uses the route below.

serverCases.name: fetch-proxy rejects a request with no X-Target-URL rather than 404ing
masked secrets list is an array of name + maskedValue
persisted set rejects a body without domains
session set rejects a body without a string value
deleting a secret that does not exist is 404, not a silent success
s3 sign-and-forward rejects an empty envelope as invalid_profile
da sign-and-forward rejects an envelope with no IMS token
sudo-approve rejects a payload with no kind — it must never prompt on garbage
